resources.title: Volunteer Researcher
resources.description: The Iakoucheva Lab at the Department of Psychiatry studies the molecular basis of autism using human in vitro 2D and 3D neuronal models. We are looking for a motivated undergraduate volunteer to participate in research aiming to elucidate the impact of copy number variants (CNVs) on neurodevelopmental phenotypes in autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and schizophrenia (SCZ).The research project focuses on studying cellular and molecular phenotypes implicated in ASD and SCZ such as neural population dynamics, dendritic and axonal outgrowth, synaptic impairment and network firing using CRISPR/Cas9-engineered isogenic human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived brain cortical organoids by utilizing techniques such as single-nuclei RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq), immunohistochemistry (IHC), multi-electrode array (MEA) and PCR.What we offer:The student will be trained in basic molecular biology techniques such as cryosectioning, immunohistochemistry and analysis of microscopy images. More advanced, cutting-edge technologies, such as snRNA-seq and MEA, as well as hands-on work with iPSCs and organoids (such as generation, maintenance, sample preparation for sequencing, etc.), will depend on the student's learning aptitude and wet lab skills.

resources.title: Research Intern
resources.description: We are currently seeking motivated and enthusiastic students interested in gaining hands-on experience in plant molecular and cellular biology, as well as gene editing. This internship offers an opportunity to work in a collaborative research environment where students will be exposed to a range of experimental techniques, including molecular cloning, plant tissue handling, DNA/RNA extraction, and basic genome editing workflows. Interns will contribute to ongoing projects, develop laboratory skills, and gain insight into experimental design, data analysis, and research practices in plant biotechnology.Ideal candidates are detail-oriented, eager to learn, and have a strong interest in plant science, molecular biology, or related fields. Prior laboratory experience is a plus but not required. This position is well-suited for students seeking to build foundational research experience and explore potential careers in academic or industry research settings.

resources.title: BS/MS: An interdisciplinary project combining epigenomics, tech-dev and human stem cells modeling of neurodevelopmental disorders
resources.description: Our interdisciplinary research focuses on regulatory genomics/epigenomics. We merge basic biology, technological innovations, and computational analyses. We are interested in understanding the role of chromatin regulation in development and disease states, such as Autism spectrum disorder and intellectual disability (ASD/ID). We are looking for a highly motivated student, with interest in molecular and computational biology that wishes to work in a dynamic, multidisciplinary research environment. We will only consider students that have maintained a minimum of 3.7 GPA and are committed, hardworking and enthusiastic. Students should be able to work for > 20 hours per week over school year and full time during the summers. The project focuses on understanding the role of the chromatin regulator SETD5 by using human stem cell and neurodifferentiation models. The student will be mentored both by Dr. Goren and Dr. Almenar-Queralt (https://profiles.ucsd.edu/angels.alhenar) and work tightly with a PhD candidate. We are highly committed to mentoring and training. This includes regular meetings (usually bi-weekly) and ad-hoc, presentation at lab meetings and other relevant opportunities when these arise (e.g., research days at school of medicine).This is an ideal BS/MS project as it involves molecular biology, next generation sequencing and computational analysis and the opportunity to author papers. The academic credit includes BSP199 and BSP196.

resources.title: Psychology Practice Intern
resources.description: Coastal Therapy Group is seeking an undergraduate student with an interest in learning both the clinical and business aspects of a private psychology practice. We value education and collaboration so we are committed to designing an experience with us that optimizes your learning objectives and the practice's needs. Through interface with our psychologists you will be exposed to a multitude of therapeutic practices (including individual, couples, and group therapy along with assessments and animal assisted therapy), therapeutic modalities (psychodynamic, relational, and skills based) diagnoses, case histories, and different clinician education and career paths. Through connection with our clients you will learn effective and empathetic communication and support skills. In the area of business you will gain an appreciation for the ethical and compliance needs of an effective practice, and the marketing strategies that make for a successful practice.Our practice can best be described as collaborative, compassionate and caring. If you are considering a career in psychology and curious about the workings of a successful psychology practice, we invite you to apply for an internship with the Coastal Therapy Group team.

resources.title: Clinical Psychology Research Assistant
resources.description: The Stress and Neuroimaging Lab at the La Jolla VA and the Neurocognition of Stress, Trauma, and Anxiety Recovery Lab at the UCSD Department of Psychiatry are looking for committed undergraduate research assistants interested in clinical psychology. The lab's studies cover a broad range of topics and generally involve functional MRI, psychiatric interviews, and a short battery of neuropsychological assessments conducted by our clinical research coordinators. The selected student research assistant would have the opportunity to assist with study tasks, such as subject recruitment, phone screening, data entry, and supporting operators during fMRI scans. Students must be willing to commit to at least 1 year of volunteering for 15 hours a week. Students who are interested in earning 199 credit are welcome to apply, but it is not required.Requirements: minimum GPA of 3.0, must be a US citizen, no criminal records. To apply, please fill out the application on our website (https://psychiatry.ucsd.edu/research/programs-centers/snl/contact/prospective-students.html) and send it to scancore.3@gmail.com in a PDF or Word document along with a CV/resume and unofficial transcript.

resources.title: Research Intern
resources.description: The Ran Lab at The Scripps Research Institute is seeking one motivated undergraduate research intern to join our team.The laboratory is interested in understanding how the brain generates internal organ sensations: the mechanical stretch of the stomach signaling fullness, toxins in the gut inducing nausea and vomiting, airway irritants triggering coughing, inflammatory or damaging signals from various organs resulting in visceral pain, and how the process of interoception goes awry in diseases including hypertension, obesity, diabetes, indigestion, pulmonary diseases, eating disorders, sleep apnea, overactive bladder, and others. Here is a description of the research https://www.ran-lab.org/.An experimental research intern will participate in the project investigating the interoceptive circuitry in the brain. The intern is expected to perform the following types of experiments: mouse behavior, mouse surgery, cryo-sectioning, microscopy, histology, physiological measurements, and computational analysis.Previous undergraduate interns and research assistants of the principal investigator have received rigorous training in science, published research articles, and been admitted to the best PhD and MD-PhD programs (including Scripps, UCSD, Stanford, UCSF, Columbia, Max Planck Institute, and others).

resources.title: Neural Circuits for motor and feeding behavior.
resources.organization: Scintillon Institute for Biomedical and Bioenergy Research
resources.description: A major goal of our laboratory is to correlate the molecular identity and connectivity of neuronal subpopulations in the nervous system with specific behaviors. Recent studies from others have uncovered neural circuits in the motor cortex, brainstem, and spinal cord that mediate skilled limb movements and locomotion, but the contribution of the cerebellar nuclei (CN) and identifiable neuronal subpopulations within CN to dexterous movement has not yet been examined. In a newly developed project that explores the ability of distinct output pathways in the CN to influence behaviors beyond motor control, we used a reverse-translational approach and screened for dysregulated neural responses to food cues and eating in humans with compulsive hyperphagia [Prader-Willi Syndrome (PWS)]. Our fMRI analysis identified neural dysregulation within the deep cerebellum of PWS individuals. To explore this functional significance, we found that activation of mouse deep cerebellar neurons dramatically decreased food intake by terminating meals earlier and reducing meal size. In brief, students will join our efforts to better understand the neural mechanisms that control dexterous movement and food intake. Projects aim to: 1) define distinctions in connectivity of motor and feeding circuits using viral tracing and genetic fate-mapping, 2) determine the role of identifiable circuits in dexterous movement and food intake through optogenetic and chemogenetic manipulation of neuronal subpopulations, 3) examine the activity profile of neural ensembles in freely moving mice using deep-brain imaging (fiber photometry or miniaturized microscopes). Visit our lab website for more information. https://www.scintillon.org/chen-home

resources.description: The UCSD Pre-professional Physical Therapy Internship is a clinically-focused experience that gives the intern access to direct patient care which is an extremely valuable and rewarding experience. Located at 9400 Campus Point Dr 2nd floor, San Diego, CA 92037. The intern will also get to learn from experts in the field of Physical Therapy and Occupational Therapy. resources.title: Analysis of the link between neural activity and behavior
resources.organization: Scintillon Institute for Biomedical and Bioenergy Research
resources.description: The Chen Lab at the Scintillon Institute is seeking undergraduate interns to participate in neurobiological research studies. The main research focus of the Chen Lab is the cerebellum, a brain structure critical to coordinating motor movements and balance, as well as contributing to learning, feeding, defensive responses, and cognitive functions. In addition to basic science research, the lab explores how cerebellar circuits are altered in diseased states. This internship position is aimed to expose students with programming/engineering backgrounds to neuroscience, and to the biotechnological methods used in neuroscience research involving rodents as a model organism. The intern will contribute to studies that involve analysis of behavioral data collected using video recordings, and neural activity signals collected using fiber photometry or miniaturized microscopes. The Scintillon Institute is a non-profit biomedical research institute located in Sorrento Valley, with research labs working on diverse fields, including neurobiology, cancer biology, metabolism, immunology. Visit our lab website for more information. https://www.scintillon.org/chen-home

Identify MRSEC trainee speakers and presenters and assist with selecting faculty speakers at MRSEC-branded seminars and events. Identify and promote opportunities for trainee professional development. Assist MRSEC leadership in identifying best practices for increasing diversity and inclusion among trainees, with focus on broadening participation and recruitment of members from groups underrepresented in STEM. In collaboration with the MRSEC faculty and staff, work to develop and sustain a welcoming and inclusive Center environment.

resources.title: Office of Research Affairs
resources.description: The Office of the Vice Chancellor for Research & Innovation (VCRI) supports, facilitates and promotes the world-class research enterprise at UC San Diego by a) providing essential services and resources that enhance research and other creative endeavors, b) enabling partnerships and collaborations among researchers at UC San Diego and between UC San Diego and government, industry and other research enterprises, and c) developing infrastructure and policy that promote innovation, an entrepreneurial culture, communication, and compliance for the UC San Diego research enterprise. The organization fosters research across disciplines by enhancing the research experience through effective stewardship of resources, policies, compliance and expertise, and by developing tools and educational programs as the responsible steward of the campus research enterprise. The Office of Research Affairs (ORA) is the central VCRI office with direct oversight for all VCRI operational, administrative and public relations/communication functions and for core units including Research and Visiting Scholars, Research Ethics, Research Initiatives, Research Proposal Development, International Outreach, and multi-disciplinary campus research (Organized Research Units). Other enterprise-wide research support departments under the Vice Chancellor for Research & Innovation include Contract and Grant Administration, Innovation and Commercialization, the Animal Care Program, Research Compliance and Integrity (IACUC, Export Control, Conflict of Interest), and the VCRI Service Core.

resources.title: Music
resources.description: Experimentation is the DNA of UC San Diego's Department of Music.Faculty and students engage with the most vital ideas and newest technologies in order to push the boundaries of musical creation and performance, and to investigate music in the context of our time.UC San Diego's Department of Music was founded by Will Ogdon and Robert Erickson in 1966. These two innovative composers shared a belief that the most effective educational environment brings together the finest faculty with gifted students in a challenging and supportive environment that encourages each student to find her or his own path.Today, the Department of Music offers graduate degree programs in Composition, Computer Music, Integrative Studies, and Contemporary Performance, and undergraduate degrees in Interdisciplinary Computing and the Arts, Music Humanities, and Music, with an emphasis in composition, literature, performance, technology, or jazz.The Department presents close to 200 events per year in our acoustically-spectacular Conrad Prebys Concert Hall, our technologically-advanced Experimental Theater, and our intimate Recital Hall. It also maintains state-of-the-art recording and research facilities equipped with the latest audio and computer technology.Resident faculty and student ensembles include: Red Fish Blue Fish (percussion); Palimpsest and Renga (new and experimental music); Kallisti (voice and chamber opera), and Jazz, Wind, Chamber, Indian, and Gospel music ensembles.The Department's faculty have won many distinguished awards, including: Pulitzer, Guggenheim, MacArthur, and Grawemeyer awards, and awards from the American Musicological Society (Colin Slim), the Society for Ethnomusicology (Alan P. Merriam), and ASCAP (Béla Bartók and Deems Taylor).Internationally renowned artists and scholars frequently visit UC San Diego for residencies to present and record new music, to provide master classes, and to share and refine new research. These guests have included: the Arditti Quartet, Muhal Richard Abrams, Robert Ashley, Richard Barrett, Han Bennink, Lisa Bielawa, John Cage, Steve Coleman, Chaya Czernowin, Brian Ferneyhough, Paul Dresher, Steven Feld, Morton Feldman, Vinko Globokar, Lydia Goehr, Fritz Hauser, Gerry Hemingway, Toshio Hosokawa, Vijay Iyer, Helmut Lachenmann, David Lang, Anne LeBaron, Joelle Leandre, George Lewis, Lisa Lim, Alvin Lucier, Miya Masaoka, Myra Melford, Nichole Mitchell, Roscoe Mitchell, Ingrid Monson, Pauline Oliveros, Hilda Paredes, Percussion Group Cincinnati, Jean-Claude Risset, Sam Rivers, Kaija Saariaho, Jaap Schroeder, Kay Kaufman Shelemay, Wadada Leo Smith, Toru Takemitsu, John Tchicai, Chou Wen-Chung, Iannis Xenikas, and Thomas Young, among others.Graduates from UC San Diego's Department of Music have been appointed to academic positions at Oxford, Stanford, Cornell, UCLA, UCI, UCSC, New York University, American University, and other prestigious institutions in the United States, and at institutions in Australia, Brazil, Canada, China, France, Finland, Hong Kong, Korea, Iceland, Ireland, Japan, Norway, Mexico, Singapore, Spain, Taiwan and the UK. Computer music students have garnered research positions with Bose Corporation, Google and Qualcomm. And composers and performers have obtained artistic positions and premieres with the International Contemporary Ensemble, the New York Philharmonic, the Los Angeles Philharmonic, London's Philharmonia Orchestra, Iceland Symphony Orchestra, Ensemble Intercontemporain, Bang on a Can, San Francisco Contemporary Music Players, CAPUT Ensemble, Oslo Philharmonic, Either/Or Ensemble, and at festivals including Lucerne, Marlboro, Darmstadt, and Tectonics.

resources.description: The UC San Diego Real Estate Department (RE) manages a multi-million-dollar portfolio of University and UC San Diego Health properties, including owned and leased assets. We negotiate and execute public/private partnerships, oversee property acquisitions and dispositions, and manage off-campus leasing. As a comprehensive real estate organization, our goal is to complete transactions on time, within budget, and to the satisfaction of our clients and The Regents of the University of California. The department is organized into three main units: (1) Property Acquisitions and Public-Private Partnerships, (2) Off-Campus Leasing, and (3) Asset Management.

resources.title: Stellar Evolution
resources.description: Stellar evolution is fundamental to astrophysics. UC San Diego researchers study a wide range of stars and substellar objects, from the coolest to the hottest, as well as the processes and outcomes of stellar death. Their research encompasses the formation and dynamics of stellar systems, the energetics of stellar explosions, and phenomena ranging from brown dwarfs to supernovae and kilonovae. Additionally, time-domain astrophysics plays a key role in observing and understanding transient stellar events. Understanding these stellar processes is crucial for comprehending planetary systems and is essential for exoplanet research at UC San Diego.

resources.title: Office of Innovation and Commercialization
resources.description: The Office of Innovation & Commercialization (OIC) has established a campus-wide innovation platform to build a systemic and sustainable innovation culture, drive social and economic prosperity through the creation of a vibrant regional ecosystem, and accelerate the commercialization of UC San Diego inventions. OIC directly supports the UC San Diego strategic plan in its vision to be a student-centered, research focused, service-oriented public university. OIC strategy supports sustainable forms of economic development through collaboration with existing industry, and the creation of new high-potential startup companies. It has established an integrated innovation platform that builds a dynamic entrepreneurial culture on campus and supports a vibrant regional ecosystem of people with diverse ideas working to develop new products, create jobs, and enrich the society we live in. Its programs increase the rate and number of university innovations that make it to the market/society and develop students who are capable of solving problems and leading and innovating in a diverse and interconnected world. OIC is responsible for a series of initiatives to drive innovation across all areas of campus and to speed university discoveries and technologies to the nation?s marketplaces. OIC includes the Intellectual Property, Commercialization Agreements, Industry Partnering, Innovation Design, and Operations units that support this enterprise.

resources.description: Library Facilities Services (LFS) provides supplemental facilities support services, directly and in liaison with campus Facilities Management, to ensure library buildings are physically functional, safe, and comfortable for users. LFS oversees material logistics for the Library, operating shipping and receiving for the Library as well as transport of library materials between locations. Coordinates space planning and management responsibilities by overseeing furniture reconfigurations, remodeling projects, and building renovations. LFS also oversees the Library Annex, an off-site storage facility for hundreds of thousands of volumes of infrequently circulated materials from the Library's collections, as well as long term storage of library files and furniture.

resources.title: Visual Arts
resources.description: The Department of Visual Arts was founded in 1966 by a highly distinguished group of conceptual artists including Paul Brach, Helen and Newton Harrison and David and Eleanor Antin, who designed the MFA curriculum around theoretical and critical issues, rather than medium and technique, as was traditional at art schools. The founders were soon joined by other leading experimental artists, including Harold Cohen, Allan Kaprow, Jerome Rothenberg, Manny Farber, Standish Lawder, Patricia Paterson, Italo Scanga, Ernie Silva and J.P. Gorin. The department quickly became known as site for advanced and experimental art with a faculty who worked across disciplines and practices - the Harrisons for their engagement with environmental science, Cohen for his pioneering work on artificial intelligence, David Antin and Rothenberg for poetry as well as performance, Eleanor Antin for writing as well as photography, video and performance, Kaprow for his theory as well as his happenings, Farber for his film criticism as well as his painting, Gorin for his writing as well as his film-making. This distinguished faculty and the innovative character of the program attracted such an extraordinary applicant pool that the alumni/ae from the first five classes alone included such widely renowned artists as Allan Sekula, Martha Rosler, Yolanda Lopez and Carrie Mae Weems, as well as Fred Lonidier, Phel Steinmetz and Kim MacConnel, who were then recruited to join the faculty. Media was an area of particular strength and Babette Mangolte and Louis Hock were recruited to teach along with Gorin, Lonidier, and Steinmetz, in a program that was often ranked as the top the nation. By the early 1980s, department artists and alumni/ae had made crucial and lasting contributions to photography, video, performance, political and environmental art, computing art, art theory and criticism, the pattern and decoration movement in painting and Chicano and border art, and the post-studio, concept-based curriculum developed and shaped at UC San Diego was imitated at other institutions.

resources.description: Learn the skills needed to become a certified personal trainer! The commitment is approximately 130 hours total.The program contains these components: Independent, online study (including quizzes and homework)In-person WorkshopsInternshipFinal written and practical examIn addition, we also require you to take 40 fitness sessions: 20 in Fall, 10 in Winter and 10 in Spring. If you successfully complete all the requirements, you will receive a certificate of completion from UC San Diego Recreation. This will make you eligible to apply for a Personal Trainer position within our department.

resources.title: HPC Student - Student Cluster Competition Team Member
resources.description: SDSC supports the Student Cluster Competition (SCC) activity, which is held at the annual Supercomputing meeting. The SCC was developed in 2007 to immerse undergraduate and high school students in high performance computing. The SCC teams consist of a mentor plus 6 students who will design and build a small cluster with support from mentors and hardware and software vendor partners. Students learn to run designated scientific applications and apply optimization techniques for their chosen architectures. SCC teams compete against teams from around the world, in a non-stop 48-hour challenge to complete a real-world scientific workload, while keeping the cluster up and running, and demonstrating to the judges their HPC skills and knowledge. Acceptance to the SC competition is competitive and requires intense preparation and skill development.San Diego Supercomputer Center (SDSC) and UC San Diego (UCSD) have sent teams to SCC since 2020, and we hope to continue the tradition.

resources.title: Atmospheric River Reconnaissance
resources.organization: Center for Western Weather and Water Extremes (CW3E)
resources.description: a. Atmospheric River Reconnaissance is a Research and Operations Partnership to collect data to improve forecasts of atmospheric rivers and associated precipitation.b. "Hurricane Hunters" from the U.S. Air Force Reserve Command 53rd Weather Reconnaissance Squadron and NOAA Office of Marine and Aviation Operations fly missions above atmospheric rivers over the Pacific.c. Flights are planned by a team of meteorologists and flight directors led by CW3E personnel.d. Flight data is complemented by data from drifting buoys, profiling floats, long-duration drifting balloons, and weather stations and balloon launches on land.e. Data collected is assimilated into global forecast systems.f. Data consistently shows significant positive impact on forecasts.

resources.title: Establishment of disease-in-a-dish model using human pluripotent stem cells (hPSC)
resources.description: Studying placenta-associated pregnancy disorders is very difficult, because disease onset happens; in vivo; in the uterus. To overcome these challenges, our group has established a model of trophoblast (placental epithelial cells) differentiation using human pluripotent stem cells (hPSC) exposed to Bone Morphogenic Protein 4 (BMP4). We found that these cells can recapitulate normal trophoblast differentiation and can be used to model abnormal differentiation.We are currently focusing on the hypertensive pregnancy disorders called preeclampsia (PE). Preeclampsia not only affects moms, but can also affect their babies during and later in their life. However, we do not have any definitive treatments for PE. We are using our hPSC disease models to understand the pathophysiology of pregnancy complications at the molecular and cellular level and to identify the pathways that can be targeted for disease interventions.

resources.title: Biomedical Engineering Society UCSD Chapter
resources.description: The BMES chapter at UCSD is a student focused organization that provides both career development opportunities and events as well as social activities and a mentorship program for all UCSD undergraduate students with an interest in bioengineering and bioengineering related fields. Anyone who falls in that category is welcome to get involved! The best way to learn about what is happening is to follow us on Instagram and sign up for our mailing list which can be found in our linktree along with the latest forms and links. Our committees are the best way to get involved and connect with other students. The event pages linked above can provide an overview of what we've done, or you can contact a committee directly to hear more about their event or what they do! At the end of each year, UCSD BMES compiles a Chapter Development Report (CDR), which we send to the National BMES Organization. Based on the CDR's from over 145 student chapters, National BMES selects one chapter to be awarded the Outstanding chapter award. We received the honor of Outstanding Chapter three times out of the past 5 years, for the 2016-2017 report, 2019-2020 report, and 2021-2022 report. To see our most recent CDR from last school year, please see here. This year, we hope to expand upon and refine our programs to make our chapter's next year even better!

resources.title: Cross-Cultural Center Internship Program, Campus Community Center
resources.description: Cross-Cultural Center Interns provide programs, services, and plan events for and with members of historically under-represented and underserved communities. Interns play a critical role in the development and operation of the CCC through front desk reception duties, facilities management, administrative tasks, educational bulletin boards, and the implementation of social justice focused education, workshops and programs. Interns learn job-related skills and the importance of teamwork, communication, and personality/working styles. They bring their knowledge of student passions, concerns, and issues to inform the Center's programs and services. Interns teach their peers about social justice concepts, current social issues and strategies for community-centered social change. The love, passion, and dedication that interns contribute to the Cross make it the ground-breaking place that it is. Every year different interns come with their own special set of interests and skills. By sharing it with the CCC, they are shaping what we are and imagining the possibilities of what we can be.

resources.title: IGPP
resources.description: The Earth Section of the Scripps Institution of Oceanography encompasses research in the Cecil H. & Ida M. Green Institute of Geophysics and Planetary Physics (IGPP) and the Geosciences Research Division (GRD). Research in IGPP spans a broad range of topics in geophysics including seismology, geodynamics, geodesy and crustal deformation, geomorphology, planetary physics, geomagnetism and paleomagnetism, oceanography and electrical methods. The Cecil and Ida Green IGPP is recognized internationally as an outstanding research and teaching institution in geophysics with focus on maintaining modern infrastructure for conducting research including buildings, computer networks, computing mass storage, seagoing instrumentation, communications and global observatories. Research in GRD embraces atmospheric, marine and solid earth chemistry, cosmochemistry, paleoceanography and paleoclimate, stratigraphy, geobiology and paleoecology, hydrogeology, global and regional tectonics, and paleomagnetism.

resources.title: Theatre and Dance
resources.description: In the 1960s, famed director Michael Langham (former head of the Guthrie Theater in Minneapolis) agreed to chair what would be a Theatre department at UCSD. At that time, a private group - the Theater and Arts Foundation - was commissioned to raise money for building a theater near the campus where Langham could launch a repertory theatre, the definitive incentive for him to settle in La Jolla. English actor and director Eric Christmas was then brought on to assist Langham for when everything was arranged. However, the money and subsequently Langham eventually fell through. Christmas stayed on, though, teaching introductory theatre courses and directing locally at the Old Globe.In 1973, UCSD finally decided to offer a major in Drama - hitherto the drama department had offered mainly introductory courses - and to pay for the construction of a theatre. Arthur Wagner was brought in in 1974 to chair the new department. Christmas would teach Acting, Floyd Gaffney was brought in to teach Dance, Stage Movement and Black Theatre, Dan Dryden would teach Technical Theatre and Design, Michael Addison taught Directing, Wagner taught Acting, Theatre History and Criticism, and Victoria Spencer served as the department's first MSO. At first a BA in Drama was offered through the school's liberal arts curriculum.A few years later, with the help of Michael Addison (who wrote the petition to the university) the graduate program was set up, offering MFAs and residencies for most of our students with La Jolla Playhouse. The department's name changed to Theatre and Dance in 1995 with the addition of the undergraduate dance studies formerly based in Physical Education led by Margaret Marshall. The evolving program offers undergraduates a Dance Major and Minor, and a Dance MFA.In 1998, UCSD Department of Theatre & Dance and UCI Department of Drama joined forces in offering a ground-breaking joint PhD in theatre history/dramatic literature that combines the faculty and resources of both campuses. Theodore and Adele Shank, with faculty and graduate students launched in 1992 the performance arts journal TheatreForum celebrating the work and published the plays of innovative theatre artists globally. TheatreForum went into hibernation in 2019 after 27 years of robust journalism. In 2019, La Jolla Playhouse began to commission the MFA graduating playwrights. Ken and Ginger Baldwin's generous philanthropy established in 1999 the Baldwin New Play Festival which showcased the MFA playwrights' work to ten professional guests nationally. The Festival - a top California venue of emerging stage talent - was renamed the Wagner Festival in 2013 when Arthur and Molli Wagner extended the Baldwin family gift for many more decades.Today, the legacy of all those who helped make the Department of Theatre & Dance what it is today lives on in the degrees offered, the facilities of Theatre District, and the various productions on stage each season. For many decades, UCSD has remained in the top rank of elite graduate theatre programs in the nation.UC San Diego Department of Theatre and Dance trains the next generation of artists and scholars who will reimagine the way we interpret our world through the performing arts.The department cultivates bold, highly talented artists capable of thriving in a variety of professional contexts. The faculty and students represent a wide range of theatrical and dance traditions and methodologies. The department encourages diversity to create work that speaks to our historical moment. The department fosters a community in which artists and scholars can realize their full potential. Production is at the core of the department's training program. It is the laboratory where the department experiments, energizes, and explores. Actors, choreographers, directors, designers, playwrights, dramaturgs and stage managers develop their skills by working on full-scale productions while being mentored by distinguished artists. The department's goal is to inspire artists and scholars with a depth of knowledge and a breadth of practice who will become leaders in the field.

resources.title: Muir College Mentorship Program
resources.description: The Muir College First-Generation Mentorship Program at UC San Diego supports the academic, social, and personal success of first-generation college students through peer mentorship, community-building, and resource sharing. Housed within Muir College Student Affairs, the program pairs continuing first-generation students with incoming first-gen mentees to foster meaningful relationships and ease the transition into college life. Through structured weekly topics, mentor training, and community events, the program encourages leadership development, cultural affirmation, and a sense of belonging. Participants engage with campus resources, learn to navigate university systems, and gain insight into personal and academic growth as part of a supportive first-gen community.

resources.title: Student Success Program
resources.description: The Library's Student Success program (SSP) fosters academic achievement and student personal growth through design and delivery of high-impact services and resources to UC San Diego's student community, with a particular focus on its undergraduate population. SSP's skilled employees collaborate with partners both across the Library and on campus to advance information literacy skills, support the holistic development of students, and represent the Library as a welcoming and inclusive space. SSP team members are trusted partners in the University's teaching mission, and use their pedagogical and other expertise to design high-impact learning experiences and co-curricular programming. Service offerings include curriculum-integrated instruction, provision of course materials, outreach focused on student well-being and belonging, assessment of the student experience, and instructional design support. The program also frequently interacts directly with a wide range of students in order to understand and enhance the student experience and encourage student use of Library space, services, and employee expertise.

resources.title: SIO Directors Office - Government Relations, Research Development, Strategic Partnerships, and Events
resources.description: The Office of Government Relations, Research Development, Strategic Partnerships, and Events provides leadership and a broad range of services to UC San Diego?s Scripps Institution of Oceanography. Through a variety of programs and activities, the office facilitates extramural funding at the federal, state and local levels, promotes strategic collaboration with external partners, and engages key external stakeholders in support of Scripps programs and goals. Program areas include research development, planning, positioning, and partnerships; government, corporate, and international relations; institutional events and venue management; and executive office analytical support. The office focuses on the following objectives: * Identify and secure opportunities and funding to advance Scripps priorities and research programs. * Develop and execute programs and activities to inform key partners and stakeholders, including research funding sponsors and government at all levels about Scripps priorities and projects. * Raise awareness of Scripps with local, national and international partners and funders and develop new strategic partnerships to advance priorities. * Create and maintain relationships with industry partners and promote innovation and technology commercialization initiatives. * Develop and execute annual plan of institutional events to increase communication and collaboration within Scripps. * Engage a variety of institutional research development, institutional positioning, and strategic planning efforts.

resources.description: The Office of Research Compliance and Integrity (RCI) facilitates research, innovation and education for global excellence and is responsible for broad oversight, resources and education for the integrity and compliance issues relating to the conduct of research. RCI has oversight and responsibility for Research Integrity and Misconduct, Conflict of Interest, the Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee Office, Export Control, Dual Use of Research Concern, Facilities Security and monitoring for Foreign Influences, Conflict of Commitment and Conflict of Interest, Good Clinical Practices training, Responsible Conduct of Research training and ClinicalTrials.gov administration as well as general research compliance monitoring and other related matters. resources.title: Seismic Design @ UCSD
resources.description: The UC San Diego Seismic Design Team provides undergraduate students with the opportunity to explore earthquake engineering through the design, build, and analysis of a 5-foot tall balsa wood model of a high-rise building. The project brings together engineering, architecture, finance and other aspects reflected in real-world projects that encourage creative thinking and facilitate learning. Every year, the team attends the Undergraduate Seismic Design Competition (SDC) hosted by the Earthquake Engineering Research Institute (EERI). The objective of the competition is to design and construct a light-weight tower that sustains minimal damage under earthquake loads, maximizes rentable floor area, and fulfills the additional guidelines provided by the EERI Student Leadership Council. These guidelines change annually based on the location of the competition in order to encourage practical and innovative ideas and to enrich the experiences of returning members.

resources.title: Marine Physical Laboratory (MPL)
resources.description: MPL was originally established as a Navy-oriented research laboratory in 1946 prior to becoming a division of Scripps Institution of Oceanography in 1949. MPL has offices both on the Scripps campus and at Navy Base Point Loma/Space and Naval Information Warfare Center (NIWC). It is the only certified facility UC-wide for classified research and holdings. Research in MPL embraces observational ocean science with emphasis on developing state of the art instrumentation for studying ocean acoustic and seismic propagation, air-sea interaction, ocean volume dynamics and ocean bottom geophysics. MPL has 31 academics in various titles (Professors, Professors in residence, Adjunct professors, Research Scientists, Project Scientists, Visiting Researchers, Specialists), 4 Research Associates/Visiting Scholars, approximately 89 staff in career, contract and limited titles, 14 postdoctoral researchers, 28 graduate students, and a large number of volunteers. MPL expends approximately $20 million annually and occupies space on- and off-campus totaling 86,800 square feet in 17 different facilities, including offices, instructional support space, and research labs.

resources.title: Supplemental Instruction (SI), Teaching and Learning Commons
resources.description: Supplemental Instruction (SI) sessions offer students the opportunity to master course material within a community of learners. The SI program gives students an environment to engage with content, ask questions, and review lecture material with their peers. SI currently supports courses in Biology, Chemistry, Economics, Math, Physics, and Psychology. Learning with a group of peers is a powerful tool! SI sessions are facilitated by peer educators (known as SI Leaders) who have successfully completed the course at UC San Diego. These leaders are trained in facilitating sessions that encourage students to work together to learn the course material. SI sessions meet weekly for 80 minutes. SI sessions are offered in a hybrid model, with both in-person and virtual sessions offered.

resources.title: Real Estate
resources.description: The UC San Diego Real Estate Department (RE) manages a multi-million-dollar portfolio of University and UC San Diego Health properties, including owned and leased assets. We negotiate and execute public/private partnerships, oversee property acquisitions and dispositions, and manage off-campus leasing. As a comprehensive real estate organization, our goal is to complete transactions on time, within budget, and to the satisfaction of our clients and The Regents of the University of California. Our team is chosen for their creativity, problem-solving skills, and real estate expertise. The department is organized into three main units: (1) Property Acquisitions and Public-Private Partnerships, (2) Off-Campus Leasing, and (3) Asset Management.

resources.title: Creative and Digital Strategy
resources.description: The University Communications Creative and Digital Strategy (CDS) department is responsible for developing creative assets and vehicles that advance UC San Diego?s reputation of prestige and distinction as a leading global research university and academic medical center. The Creative and Digital Strategy department is made up of six distinct teams: design, project management and editorial, digital strategy, photography, video, and UC San Diego Magazine. Staff members work collaboratively as a team of professionals who identify and leverage new tools to engage, inspire, and galvanize key constituencies. The department also operates two full-featured video and photography studios for video recording, podcasting, photography, and broadcast productions. Employing best practices in research, planning, execution, and measurement, CDS team members bring curiosity and agility to creating digital, print, photo, video, and graphic assets that contribute to the university?s short- and long-term strategic and operational objectives. Members of the CDS department also serve as key advisers to University Communications and campus leaders and facilitate cross-functional collaboration.

resources.title: Geosciences Research Division (GRD)
resources.description: The Earth Section of the Scripps Institution of Oceanography encompasses research in the Cecil H. & Ida M. Green Institute of Geophysics and Planetary Physics (IGPP) and the Geosciences Research Division (GRD). Research in IGPP spans a broad range of topics in geophysics including seismology, geodynamics, geodesy and crustal deformation, geomorphology, planetary physics, geomagnetism and paleomagnetism, oceanography, and electrical methods. The Cecil and Ida Green IGPP is recognized internationally as an outstanding research and teaching institution in geophysics with a focus on maintaining modern infrastructure for conducting research including buildings, computer networks, computing mass storage, seagoing instrumentation, communications, and global observatories. Research in GRD embraces atmospheric, marine, and solid earth chemistry, cosmochemistry, paleoceanography and paleoclimate, stratigraphy, geobiology and paleoecology, hydrogeology, global and regional tectonics, and paleomagnetism.

resources.title: Collection Development & Management Program
resources.description: The Collection Development & Management Program (CDM) supports and advances the university?s mission of research, teaching, and public service by selecting, managing, and preserving information resources across all relevant disciplines. The program?s ultimate goal is to provide our primary user community with access to the information they need, when and where they need it, and in the form most useful to them. The program plays a critical role in supporting the cycle of knowledge through ongoing stewardship of the products of research (collections and content). We select content to purchase, using a variety of acquisition methods to maximize the reach of our funding and meet needs of users. We work with physical collections, curating the content to keep it relevant to user needs, and preserving the materials to extend its lifecycle for as long as possible.

resources.title: Embedded Writing Mentor Program, Analytical Writing Program
resources.description: The Analytical Writing Program (AWP) at the University of California San Diego offers writing classes that fulfill the UC Entry Level Writing Requirement (ELWR). The program also administers the UC San Diego Writing Placement Process and offers a range of courses that develop students' critical thinking, reading, and writing skills. The program places Embedded Writing Mentors in AWP classes to provide students with individualized support. The writing mentors help students develop good topics, construct strong and interesting questions and claims, organize and support their arguments, and craft clear and coherent sentences and paragraphs. AWP's courses help our diverse population of students focus on improving their writing, learning, and practicing academic writing skills that will prepare them to succeed in all of the College Writing Programs and beyond. Students write regular short writing assignments that build the foundation for Summary & Synthesis and Argument essays. Students focus on revision as a process, ultimately revising their drafts multiple times in order to produce a strong portfolio at the end of the course. The Embedded Writing Mentor Program (EWMP) was created to provide students in AWP with one-on-one mentoring to help students reflect on their writing process with highly trained peers.More information can be found at https://awp.ucsd.edu/.

resources.title: Birch Aquarium at Scripps
resources.description: Birch Aquarium is a public aquarium in La Jolla, a community of San Diego, California. It serves as the public outreach center for Scripps Institution of Oceanography at the University of California, San Diego, with over half a million people visiting the aquarium each year. The aquarium houses more than 3,000 animals representing over 380 species. The hilltop site provides views of La Jolla Shores and the Pacific Ocean. The aquarium is an accredited member of the Association of Zoos and Aquariums (AZA).

resources.title: Natural Reserve System
resources.description: The University of California San Diego Natural Reserve System (NRS) manages four of the 42 field stations that make up the largest and most diverse set of university-affiliated reserves in the world. The reserves include examples of most major ecosystems in the state. They provide secure sites for research, instruction, and public outreach. They enable monitoring of environmental health and provide a baseline for ecosystem restoration in the context of California's rapidly growing population and the changing global environment. UC San Diego Natural Reserve System sites include: • Scripps Coastal Reserve • Kendall-Frost Marsh Reserve • Dawson-Los Monos Reserve • Elliott Chaparral Reserve

resources.title: Business Intelligence and People Systems
resources.description: Business & Financial Services (BFS) is the major business operation directed by the Assistant Vice Chancellor / UC San Diego Controller. The Office of the Controller provides leadership, consultation, promotion, accountability, encouragement, and expertise in building and maintaining an effective control environment. This environment is exemplified by effective business practices; well-trained and knowledgeable staff; ethical behavior, separation of duties, timely and complete communication; well-defined and understandable policy; effective risk identification and management; and quality results. Ultimately, this leads to the effective use of university resources and accurate and complete financial statements fairly reflect the results of university operations. Many programs and initiatives to ensure such an environment is in effect are developed and deployed from this office. Many of the major business processes for the campus are operated by various divisions of this department. Each division of BFS is led by a director that reports to executives within the Office of the Controller. These divisions include Financial Operations, Business Intelligence & Financial Reporting, Costing Policy & Analysis, Finance & Budget, Office of the Controller, Sponsored Projects Finance, Internal Controls & Accounting, IPPS (Disbursements & Travel, Mail Services, Logistics, Procurement & Contracts), Student Financial Solutions (Student Business Services & Central Cashiers') and Organizational Excellence. There are nearly 300 career and 100+ student employees and located in five different facilities that comprise Business & Financial Services. There are also a relatively small number of contractors and casual employees. The operations of this department encompass all campus departments and schools, but for the most part, do not include the fiscal operations of the Medical Centers, the Medical Group Clinics, or the UC San Diego Foundation.

resources.title: Enrollment Management, Office of Undergraduate Admissions
resources.description: The Office of Undergraduate Admissions leads the university's efforts to identify, recruit, admit and enroll the next generation of UC San Diego Tritons with particular focus on talented, academically capable, California students, representative of the diversity of the people of California. The mission of the office includes increasing the visibility of UC San Diego in California, the nation and world, through marketing and on- and off- campus recruitment activities to prospective first-year and transfer students and their families; school counselors; community college leaders and advisors; community based organizations; and educational organizations serving groups historically underrepresented on our campus. The Office of Undergraduate Admissions hosts more than 80,000 visitors and receives, processes, and reviews over 150,000 applications for admission annually. The office works collaboratively with on-and off- campus partners to achieve university goals.

The program includes engagement with Native American and historically marginalized communities, as well as fieldwork in and around California's national and state parks and other natural settings. Through these on-site experiences, MMW Serves fosters a deeper understanding of human and environmental landscapes and their interconnection. The AY25-26 Program took place in California's Colorado Desert region.

resources.title: Enrollment Management, Financial Aid & Scholarships Office
resources.description: The Financial Aid and Scholarships (FAS) Office works collaboratively with the rest of Enrollment Management and other campus partners to support students from their recruitment, initial enrollment and through degree completion. The office works to ensure all admitted and continuing students have adequate financial resources available to attend UC San Diego. The FAS Office administers over $550 million in support to undergraduate students and $15 million to graduate/professional level students (excluding Health Sciences). About 70% of undergraduates receive some form of support, with this number growing each year. The staff provides outreach services, counseling, eligibility and verification determination, budgeting, awarding, reconciliation of payments, and federal, state, and university reporting.

resources.title: Lagrangrian Drifter Laboratory (LDL)
resources.organization: Climate, Atmosphere Sciences, and Physical Oceanography (CASPO)
resources.description: The Lagrangian Drifter Laboratory (LDL) develops tools, methods, and instruments that are used to collect Lagrangian ocean velocity and other oceanographic parameters in the coastal and global oceans in support of oceanographic research. Activities of the LDL cover a wide scope, including instrument and experiment design, electronic and mechanical engineering, instrument construction, execution of field experiments, management of real-time data flows, data processing, and collaborations with national and international colleagues on scientific research.
